paragraphs.title: The Symbolic Belt and Its Ruin

easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Jeremiah to get a linen girdle.
easy.q: What was Jeremiah commanded to buy?

answers: In a hole of the rock by Euphrates
easy.explanation: He was told to hide it in a hole of the rock by Euphrates.
easy.q: Where was Jeremiah told to hide the girdle?

answers: It was marred and profitable for nothing
easy.explanation: The girdle was marred and no longer useful.
easy.q: What condition was the girdle in when Jeremiah retrieved it?

answers: He got it, wore it, hid it, and retrieved it
He hid it, got it, wore it, and retrieved it
He retrieved it, wore it, got it, and hid it
medium.explanation: Jeremiah first got and wore the girdle, then hid it and later retrieved it.
medium.q: What was the order of Jeremiah's actions?

answers: An opening or hollow in the rock
medium.explanation: A hole of the rock is an opening or hollow within the rock.
medium.q: What does the KJV phrase “a hole of the rock” mean?

answers: It had been soaked in water
It had torn during his journey
It had been hidden for many days and became damaged
medium.explanation: The girdle was hidden for many days and was later found marred.
medium.q: Why was the girdle ruined by the time Jeremiah retrieved it?

answers: To show the future condition of the people
To explain how linen was made
challenge.explanation: The ruined girdle served as a sign of the people's future condition.
challenge.q: What was the symbolic purpose of the girdle?

answers: He asked the people for advice
He did according to the word of the Lord
He exchanged the girdle for another garment
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah repeatedly did what the Lord commanded him.
challenge.q: Which detail especially shows Jeremiah's obedience?

answers: Something close and useful can become ruined through separation and neglect
challenge.explanation: The girdle was first worn closely but later became useless after being hidden.
challenge.q: What contrast is shown by the girdle's condition?

paragraphs.title: The Meaning: The People's Separation from God

answers: The pride of Judah and Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The Lord said He would mar the pride of Judah and Jerusalem.
They were described as an evil people who refused to hear God's words.
easy.q: What did the people refuse to do?

easy.explanation: They walked after other gods, served them, and worshipped them.

answers: Both had failed to fulfill their intended purpose
medium.explanation: The useless girdle represented a people who had rejected their proper purpose.
medium.q: What connection did the Lord make between the girdle and the people?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes following one's own thoughts and desires instead of God's word.
medium.q: What does “the imagination of their heart” mean in this passage?

answers: To be His people, His name, His praise, and His glory
medium.explanation: The Lord intended them to be His people, name, praise, and glory.
medium.q: For what purpose had the Lord caused Israel and Judah to cleave unto Him?

answers: Closeness to God versus refusal to hear Him
challenge.explanation: The people were meant to remain close to God but refused to hear Him.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in this passage?

answers: It was used for carrying wine
It cleaved closely to a person's loins, as the people were meant to cleave to God
It was always worn in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The girdle's closeness pictured the closeness God intended for His people.
challenge.q: Why was a girdle an appropriate symbol for the people?

answers: They became like the girdle that was good for nothing
challenge.explanation: Their refusal led to a condition represented by the ruined and useless girdle.
challenge.q: What resulted from the people's refusal to hear?

short_answers.question: In one short phrase, what did the girdle represent?
answers: The pride of Judah and Jerusalem
short_answers.explanation: The girdle represented the pride of Judah and Jerusalem.

paragraphs.title: The Metaphor of the Wine Jars and Drunkenness

easy.explanation: The Lord said that every bottle would be filled with wine.
easy.q: With what were all the bottles to be filled?

answers: The inhabitants of the land, including its leaders
easy.explanation: The kings, priests, prophets, and inhabitants of Jerusalem would be filled with drunkenness.
easy.q: Whom would the Lord fill with drunkenness?

answers: They would be dashed one against another
They would all flee to Euphrates
easy.explanation: The Lord said He would dash them one against another.
easy.q: What would happen to the people against one another?

answers: Because the simple statement pointed to a more serious message
Because there were no clay bottles
Because wine was forbidden to priests
medium.explanation: Their question allowed the Lord to explain the symbolic meaning of the bottles.
medium.q: Why did the people ask whether they already knew that every bottle would be filled with wine?

medium.explanation: Here drunkenness pictures confusion, trouble, and judgment.
medium.q: What does “drunkenness” represent in this passage?

answers: The land would be filled with new clay vessels
He would fill the inhabitants of the land with drunkenness
The people would fill Jerusalem with wine
medium.explanation: The bottles represented the people who would be filled with drunkenness.
medium.q: How did the Lord explain the bottle metaphor?

answers: Both describe something filling a vessel or a whole land
challenge.explanation: The physical filling of bottles illustrates the spreading of judgment throughout the land.
challenge.q: What is the connection between filling the bottles with wine and filling the land with drunkenness?

answers: Every level of society would share in the trouble
challenge.explanation: The list includes kings, priests, prophets, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What does the list of people affected by drunkenness emphasize?

answers: The destruction would be severe and without mercy
The people could immediately repair their condition
challenge.explanation: The repeated denial of pity and mercy emphasizes the seriousness of the judgment.
challenge.q: What added severity comes from the statement that the Lord would not pity, spare, or have mercy?

paragraphs.title: A Call to Listen and Repent

easy.explanation: They were told to hear and give ear because the Lord had spoken.
easy.q: What were the people commanded to hear and give ear to?
What attitude were they warned against?

answers: Because the Lord's flock would be carried away captive
Because the southern cities were closed
easy.explanation: Jeremiah would weep because the Lord's flock would be taken captive.
easy.q: Why would the prophet weep if the people would not hear?

answers: Give glory to the Lord their God
Hide in a hole of the rock
medium.explanation: They were urged to give glory to God before the coming darkness.
medium.q: What were the people to do before darkness came?

medium.explanation: The command warns the people against pride and self-exaltation.
medium.q: What does “be not proud” mean in this context?

answers: It offered an opportunity to honor God and change
It would help fill the bottles
It would open the cities of the south
medium.explanation: The warning gave the people an opportunity to respond before judgment came.
medium.q: How could listening affect the coming darkness?

challenge.explanation: Darkness and stumbling on the dark mountains picture coming trouble.
challenge.q: What does darkness symbolize in this passage?

answers: He grieved because the Lord's flock would be carried away
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah's tears reveal his grief over the people's captivity.
challenge.q: Why does the prophet's weeping show that his warning was not spoken coldly?

answers: Pride prevents listening, so the people fail to turn in time
Pride causes the bottles to be filled
challenge.explanation: The people were urged to abandon pride and listen before disaster arrived.
challenge.q: How are pride and the coming disaster connected?

paragraphs.title: The Humbling of the Royal House and Exile

easy.explanation: The king and queen were commanded to humble themselves and sit down.
easy.q: Who was told to humble themselves?

easy.explanation: Their principalities would come down, including the crown of their glory.
easy.q: What happened to the crown of their glory?

easy.explanation: Judah would be wholly carried away captive.

answers: Their authority and glory were about to be brought down
They were preparing for a feast
They needed to hide a girdle
medium.explanation: Their royal authority would be humbled and their crown brought down.
medium.q: Why were the king and queen told to humble themselves?

answers: Your high position and authority will be brought low
Your wine vessels will be filled
Your city gates will be opened
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the lowering of royal rank and power.
medium.q: What does “your principalities shall come down” mean?

answers: A loss of freedom and security
medium.explanation: The shut cities and captivity show that Judah lost freedom and security.

answers: The success of the royal house
The humiliation and loss of royal glory
The actual choosing of a new king
challenge.explanation: The fallen crown symbolized the humiliation of the royal house.
challenge.q: What did the removal of the crown symbolize?

answers: Judah would have to answer for her conduct
Judah was about to receive a gift
challenge.explanation: The question calls Judah to account for her actions and leadership.
challenge.q: What is implied by the question, “What wilt thou say when he shall punish thee?”

answers: Forgetting God and trusting falsehood led to the exposure of Judah's shame
challenge.explanation: Judah's unfaithfulness and trust in falsehood resulted in her sins being exposed.
challenge.q: How are forgetting God and public shame connected in the final verses?

short_answers.question: In one short phrase, what happened to Judah?
short_answers.explanation: The KJV says that Judah would be wholly carried away captive.

short_answers.question: In one short phrase, what did Judah forget?
short_answers.explanation: The Lord said that Judah had forgotten Him.
